correctness.rationale: Both coordinate graphs are vertex-transitive. Independent exact neighbor checks give degree six, two common neighbors per distinct pair, and local 2-regular graphs with two and zero triangles respectively, distinguishing the isomorphism types. Thus A²=4I+2J, so A has eigenvalues 6, 2, −2 of multiplicities 1, 6, 9, and D=2(J−I)−A gives 24, −4, 0 with the same multiplicities. I independently computed rooted simple paths by the reverse recurrence f(U,w)=sum of f(U minus w,j) over j adjacent to w in U minus w, with f({0},0)=1 and no other path ending at its own start. Deleting the last edge is a bijection, so this exhausts the ordered nonempty simple paths at all lengths 1–15. All 30 entries match RESULT.md, including 34452 and 34320 at the first differing length seven. (Total paths, total lengths) are (13991682,177310488) and (14029326,177724236); the exact reduced quotient difference is 24601265726/5452607446287. Vertex transitivity gives F=cI−D, yielding the stated eigenvalues; the distinct traces alone prove separation.
residual_risks: Counts depend on excluding the zero-edge path and distinguishing paths as ordered from a fixed root, as in the stated definition. No other graph pair is inferred.

originality.rationale: The novel claim supported here is the exact all-length weighted mean difference for this pair and the resulting average-flow spectral separation. Prior work has the scalar shift, the graph pair, and a path-multiset separation through length seven. Those do not establish that the weighted mean survives cancellation across lengths. No complete prior table or stronger covering result was established in the inspected material.
residual_risks: Unindexed rooted-path tables or an equivalent all-length aggregation remain possible, and a later rediscovery must check such evidence. The literature query was not informative; its irrelevant results are not negative evidence.

value.rationale: The rook and Shrikhande graphs are a canonical test of graph invariants: both are vertex-transitive and have identical adjacency and distance spectra. It is worthwhile to know whether the single scalar contributed by the new average-flow matrix actually distinguishes this pair after summing all lengths, since known path-based distinctions need not survive that aggregation. The exact nonzero shift is a counterexample to sameness of average-flow spectra for distance-cospectral graphs and provides a reproducible numerical benchmark. The finite count is motivated by that question, not by a randomly chosen pair or the numerical size of the gap.
residual_risks: This demonstrates a particular direction of separation on one distinguished pair, not general injectivity or a classification.
